validity.recommendation: none needed for existence/classification/route/duplicate — this is one of the best-corroborated rows in the country, real and correctly classified
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: unambiguously real, and about as thoroughly independently documented as any pipeline in this tracker. The Soyuz («Soyuz» / Союз) trunk line is (1) the subject of a dedicated, detailed ru.wikipedia infobox article (construction 1975–1979, commissioned 11 Nov 1980, route Orenburg–Uralsk–Aleksandrov Gay–Sokhranivka GIS (RU/UA border)–Kremenchug–Dolyna–Uzhhorod, length 2750 km incl. 300 km in Kazakhstan + 1568 km in Ukraine), (2) independently described with matching route/history/capacity by Neftegaz.ru's technical library (built 1975-1979 by the USSR + Comecon partners, commissioned 1980, gas from the Orenburg field, capacity 26 bn m3/y), (3) by fb.ru (same route/history, capacity 26 bn m3/y, one of the USSR's main Cold-War gas export trunks alongside Bratstvo/Progress/Urengoy-Pomary-Uzhhorod), (4) confirmed at the Ukraine-segment level by English Wikipedia's heavily-footnoted 'Natural gas transmission system of Ukraine' article, citing the Naftogaz/Ukrtransgas priority-investment master plan documents directly (Ukraine section length 1,567 km — matching ru.wikipedia's 1568 km to within rounding; capacity 26.1 bn m3/y; enters Ukraine via the Sokhranivka GIS east of Novopskov, leaves via the Uzhhorod GIS/pumping station), (5) confirmed at the official-statistics level by cdu.ru (Russia's Central Fuel-Energy-Complex Dispatch Directorate), which lists 'Soyuz — 25.2 bn m3/y of Russian gas' — an EXACT match to GEM's own Capacity value, (6) confirmed at the Kazakhstan-segment level by Intergas Central Asia JSC's own official 'General Information' page, which lists the Soyuz MGP as part of its Uralsk Branch network, and (7) confirmed historically by a scholarly book snippet (Google Books) discussing the 1974 Comecon Orenburg pipeline financing agreement that produced this line. None of these are gem.wiki, GEM, or banned sources. CLASSIFICATION: PipelineType=transmission and Fuel=Gas are both correct — every source describes it as a 'main/trunk gas pipeline' (магистральный газопровод), one of the USSR's flagship natural-gas export trunks — not a gathering/feeder/process line. ROUTE/ENDPOINTS: StartLocation=Orenburg/Russia and EndLocation=Uzhgorod/Ukraine are both correct per every source (note the pipeline also transits ~300 km of Kazakhstan between the two, which the sheet's Start/End fields do not need to capture). DUPLICATE: checked against the full 6-pipeline roster (P0788 Ostrogozhsk-Shebelinka, P0793 Stavropol-Moscow, P1457 Taganrog-Mariupol-Berdyansk, P1487 Poland-Ukraine Interconnector, P1773 Romania-Ukraine Interconnector) — none share Soyuz's Orenburg–Kazakhstan–Ukraine(Sokhranivka–Kremenchug–Dolyna)–Uzhhorod corridor or its scale (2750 km / 1420 mm / 25–26 bcm/y); no duplicate within this roster. For the record (not a roster duplicate, just context): cdu.ru's own list shows Soyuz is DISTINCT from the parallel, smaller 'Orenburg–Novopskov' pipeline (14.6 bn m3/y) that runs alongside it up to Novopskov — don't conflate the two if either surfaces later.

validity.recommendation: no change to Capacity/Diameter, but note the sourcing profile in ResearcherNotes: capacity has a genuine design-vs-actual spread and diameter rests on one strong explicit source
validity.researcher_notes: CAPACITY: GEM's 25.20 bcm/y is an EXACT match to Russia's official cdu.ru (Central Dispatch Directorate of the Fuel & Energy Complex) figure of '25,2 млрд куб. м в год' for the Soyuz line specifically — this is a strong, independent, authoritative confirmation and I would NOT change the value. However, three other independent sources (ru.wikipedia's infobox 'design capacity', neftegaz.ru, fb.ru) all cite a rounder '26 bn m3/y' design/nameplate figure, and en.wikipedia's Naftogaz-master-plan-sourced figure for the Ukraine segment specifically is 26.1 bn m3/y. This ~3% spread (25.2 vs 26/26.1) is the ordinary design-vs-actual-technical-capacity variance seen across Soviet-era trunks and is NOT treated as a material conflict requiring a value change — but it is real enough that I would not silently treat 25.2 as the only number that exists; flagging it rather than picking a winner. DIAMETER: GEM's 1420.00 mm is confirmed explicitly by ru.wikipedia's infobox ('Диаметр 1420 мм'), which is entirely consistent with 1420 mm being the standard USSR 'super-power' export-trunk diameter class used on the parallel Urengoy-Pomary-Uzhhorod and Progress lines of the same era and capacity class. I could not independently corroborate the exact 1420 mm figure on a second source distinct from ru.wikipedia within this pass (neftegaz.ru and fb.ru describe the route/history/capacity but do not state diameter) — tier medium rather than high on diameter specifically, not because I found any conflicting figure, but because a second explicit citation is still worth chasing in a future pass.

validity.recommendation: the three named parties (Gas TSO of Ukraine / Gazprom PJSC / QazaqGaz + operating subsidiary Intergas Central Asia) are each independently correct for this genuinely tri-national line, but the Owner percentage split (Owner1=TSOU 100%, Owner2=Gazprom blank%, Owner3=QazaqGaz blank%) is internally inconsistent — 100% cannot be assigned to one owner while two more owners are also listed; recommend re-expressing this as segment-based ownership (each state entity owns ~100% of its own national section) in ResearcherNotes rather than as fractional co-ownership of one asset, or leaving all three percentages blank
validity.researcher_notes: This is a genuinely cross-border line (Russia→Kazakhstan→Ukraine, per the existence findings above), so — unlike a wholly-domestic Ukrainian row — having Gazprom PJSC listed alongside Ukraine's TSOU is NOT itself the attribution red flag the country guidance warns about; it reflects the real multi-country asset. Checked piece by piece: (a) Ukraine's Gas TSO of Ukraine (TSOU) as post-2020 operator of the Ukrainian section is independently confirmed by en.wikipedia's well-footnoted 'Natural gas transmission system of Ukraine' article ('The system is owned by Government of Ukraine and operated by Gas Transmission System Operator of Ukraine'); (b) Intergas Central Asia JSC as operator of the Kazakhstan section is confirmed by its own official 'General Information' page, which lists the Soyuz MGP under its Uralsk Branch network; (c) QazaqGaz as Intergas Central Asia's 100%-owning parent is confirmed by QazaqGaz's own official corporate-structure page, which lists 'Intergas Central Asia JSC' under its 'Trunk transportation' subsidiaries; (d) Gazprom's role on the Russian section is supported more weakly — ru.wikipedia's navbox categorizes Soyuz among Gazprom's Russian main export trunks ('Магистральные газопроводы России' / 'Gazprom pipeline map'), which is standard but indirect. Given all three parties check out individually, I filled the Operator ref with these sources rather than marking UNRESOLVED, but the ownership PERCENTAGE structure (100% / blank / blank) is a real data-model inconsistency that predates this pass and that I could not resolve to a defensible split — I did not fabricate percentages for Owner2/Owner3, and I would not paste any percentage change without a source that states an actual ownership share (none of my sources state one; they state operator/subsidiary roles, not equity splits).

fills.researcher_notes: 'mothballed' is well supported: ru.wikipedia documents that the Sokhranivka gas metering station — the Soyuz line's only entry point from Russia into Ukraine — has been closed to transit since May 2022 (Ukraine cited loss of control/interference in Russian-occupied Luhansk territory), and biz.liga.net (2025-01-01) documents that the entire remaining Russia-Ukraine transit arrangement (via the Sudzha entry point, used by other lines after Sokhranivka closed) ended on schedule 2025-01-01 when the 2019 transit contract expired unrenewed. So Soyuz's transit function has had zero throughput since May 2022 and the whole transit corridor it belongs to has been formally dead since 2025-01-01 — consistent with, and supportive of, 'mothballed' rather than 'operating'.
Both sources describe Soyuz as a natural gas trunk pipeline carrying gas from the Orenburg gas-condensate field ('магистральный газопровод'). No ambiguity.

Both a Russian technical library entry and the English-language Ukraine GTS article treat Soyuz as one of the country's main interstate transmission trunks (grouped with Urengoy-Pomary-Uzhhorod and Progress) — not a gathering/feeder/process line.

ru.wikipedia's infobox gives an exact commissioning date, 'начало эксплуатации 11 ноября 1980 года' (11 November 1980), and neftegaz.ru corroborates the year ('газопровод принят в эксплуатацию в 1980 г.'). Adding StartMonth1=11 as a deep-fill on the strength of the one explicit-date source; the year itself (1980) is corroborated twice. Note fb.ru gives a slightly different CONSTRUCTION window (1975–1976 vs the other two sources' 1975–1979) — minor and not relevant to StartYear1, which is the commissioning date, not the construction start.

cdu.ru (Russia's official Central Fuel-Energy-Complex Dispatch Directorate) states 'Soyuz (Russian gas; 25.2 bn m3/y)' verbatim — an exact match to GEM's value. Tier set to medium rather than high because the other 3 independent sources found (ru.wikipedia, neftegaz.ru, fb.ru, en.wikipedia) cluster around a distinct '26 / 26.1 bn m3/y' design figure rather than replicating 25.2 exactly — see the paired 'spec' validity finding for the full discussion. Not proposing a value change; flagging the spread.

ru.wikipedia states the total length as exactly '2750 км' with a country breakdown (300 km Kazakhstan, 1568 km Ukraine, remainder — ~882 km — Russia). en.wikipedia's separately-footnoted (Naftogaz master-plan-sourced) figure for the Ukraine segment alone, '1,567 kilometres', matches ru.wikipedia's 1568 km component to within 1 km rounding — two independently-sourced figures agreeing on the largest sub-component is strong corroboration for the 2750 km total.

ru.wikipedia's infobox states 'Диаметр 1420 мм' exactly. Single explicit source this pass (see paired 'spec' validity finding); 1420 mm is the standard diameter class for USSR-era super-trunk export lines of this capacity, so plausibility is high even though a second explicit citation wasn't found.

Both sources name the Orenburg gas-condensate field ('Оренбургское месторождение') as the resource base ('ресурсная база') for the line, matching the sheet exactly; a third source (fb.ru) independently agrees.

en.wikipedia states the Soyuz pipeline 'originat[es] from the Orenburg gas field' and 'leaves Ukraine through the Uzhhorod gas metering and pumping station' — confirming both endpoints exactly as recorded. Deep-filling the previously-blank EndState/Province with 'Zakarpattia Oblast' — Uzhhorod is that oblast's administrative center (en.wikipedia's Uzhhorod article), a trivial, unambiguous geographic fact. Not filling Start/EndPrefecture/District (no district-level claim needed/found).

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Searched extensively (Russian + Ukrainian) for any 2024-2026 news specific to the Soyuz line and to the Sokhranivka crossing it uses. Findings, newest first: (1) biz.liga.net, 2025-01-01: the entire 2019 Russia-Ukraine transit agreement expired unrenewed at 07:00 on 2025-01-01, ending ALL remaining gas transportation from Russia's Sudzha entry point westward through Ukraine — the last live transit route in the system Soyuz belongs to. (2) A neftegaz.ru news item (2024, headline 'Applications for Russian gas transit via Ukraine's GTS fell 25%. However, Sokhranovka...') indicates Gazprom was still filing daily nomination requests at the Sokhranivka station through 2024 and Naftogaz was rejecting them — i.e., ZERO flow via Soyuz's own entry point continuously since May 2022, well before the 2025-01-01 full stoppage. (3) ru.wikipedia and multiple corroborating sources confirm the Sokhranivka GIS — Soyuz's sole Russia→Ukraine crossing — has been shut to transit since May 2022 because it sits in Russian-occupied Luhansk territory. Net effect: Soyuz has carried no Russia-to-Ukraine transit gas since May 2022 (over 4 years), and the broader corridor it feeds has been formally dead since 2025-01-01. This is squarely 'mothballed' (physically intact, not decommissioned, simply unused for its transit function amid the war) rather than 'operating' (no current flow) or 'retired' (no evidence of decommissioning/dismantling — the standing country guidance explicitly warns against inferring retirement from the general transit-halt fact alone, and I found no line-specific decommissioning evidence). I did not find any indication Soyuz still moves domestic Ukrainian or reverse-flow gas on its Ukraine section independent of the Russia-sourced transit function, so I'm confirming the existing status as-is rather than proposing a change.

summary: P0761 Soyuz Gas Pipeline: real, correctly classified, no duplicate within the 6-pipeline roster — among the best-corroborated rows in the country (7 independent, non-wiki-GEM sources); filled all 9 missing MISSING_REF cells (Status/Fuel/PipelineType/Start+Month/Capacity/Length/Diameter/FuelSource/Location) plus the Operator ref, all REFS_ADDED; two caveats flagged (not concerns): capacity clusters 25.2 (cdu.ru, exact GEM match) vs 26/26.1 elsewhere (design-vs-actual spread, no change proposed), and the Owner% split (TSOU 100% / Gazprom blank / QazaqGaz blank) is internally inconsistent for this genuinely tri-national line and needs a data-model fix, not a fabricated percentage; status 'mothballed' CONFIRMED (evidence through 2025-01: Sokhranivka entry closed since May 2022, full transit corridor dead since 2025-01-01).
